text: attachControl's drag, wheel and keys only add to the camera's inertial*Offset fields; alpha, beta, radius and target change only when the scene's _beforeRender runs. Without the scene argument the camera never moves (pinch excepted).
fails_if: Drag and wheel input would change alpha or radius at once, or the camera would move without a scene.

text: Limit fields (upperRadiusLimit etc.) written straight onto a camera clamp no write until setCameraLimits has been called on it: radius = 50 with upperRadiusLimit 12 stays 50. interpolateArcRotateCamera clamps its goals to them anyway.
fails_if: A directly written limit field would clamp radius on write or during attachControl's frames, or interpolateArcRotateCamera would not settle on it.

text: setCameraLimits clamps the current pose at once; from then on each write that changes alpha/beta/radius is clamped in the same statement, using the limit fields as they are then, and zeroes that inertial offset only if it hit a bound.
fails_if: Clamping would wait for a frame, ignore later limit fields, apply on a same-value write, or zero the offset on a write inside the limits.

text: Each geospatial yaw/pitch/radius write clamps pitch against the radius at that moment; by default pitch is forced to 0.001 at radius >= 4*planetRadius, so pitch = 1 at the start is lost. Use setGeospatialOrientation({pitch, radius}).
fails_if: pitch = 1 at the starting radius would be kept, or a later radius write would restore it.

text: Projection is reverse-Z with depth in [0,1]: a point at nearPlane gets depth 1 and one at farPlane depth 0, also in projectWorldToScreen's z.
fails_if: Depth would grow from near to far, or use [-1,1].

text: createArcRotateCamera sets nearPlane 0.1 and farPlane 1000 (createFreeCamera: 1 and 10000), fov 0.8, and panningSensibility 50.
fails_if: The arc-rotate camera would start with other near/far planes or another panningSensibility.

text: An ArcRotate camera's target is an observable vector: write target.x/y/z in place. Assigning a new object to camera.target leaves worldMatrix stale until a write changes alpha, beta or radius; that uses the object as it is then.
fails_if: Assigning camera.target = {...} would move the world matrix at once, or the next changing radius/alpha write would not use the new object.

text: Free-camera controls steer by _yaw/_pitch, which are computed only at creation. A target written later is replaced on the next control move or turn by position + unit look vector from the old yaw/pitch.
fails_if: After a written target, the next control move would keep that look direction.

text: attachControl's keyboard: true is ignored unless enableArcRotateKeyboardControls() ran first. Keys are heard on the canvas (tabIndex made 0 if no tabindex attribute); held arrows add 1/angularSensitivity (default 100) per frame, normalised.
fails_if: keyboard: true would install listeners without the enable call, keys would act on keydown, two arrows would not be normalised, or an existing tabindex would be overwritten.

text: interpolateArcRotateCamera zeroes the inertial offsets on its first frame, then rejects with an 'interrupted' Error if anything else changes alpha, beta, radius or target between frames: a drag, a direct write, or a newer interpolation.
fails_if: The promise would resolve or keep going when the pose is changed from outside, or would leave inertial offsets in place.

text: getViewMatrix, getProjectionMatrix and getViewProjectionMatrix return the camera's own cache array, overwritten in place on the next call after a change; copy it to keep a value.
fails_if: A later call after a change would return a new array or leave the earlier one unchanged.

text: An ArcRotate camera has no beta limits by default; attachControl's frame step clamps beta to [0.01, PI-0.01], but only on frames where inertialAlphaOffset or inertialBetaOffset is non-zero. beta = 0 written directly stays 0.
fails_if: beta would be clamped without rotation inertia, by a default lowerBetaLimit, or to other bounds.

text: attachControl's wheel does inertialRadiusOffset -= deltaY*radius/(wheelPrecision*1000) and each frame radius -= that offset, so positive deltaY zooms out, in steps proportional to radius; radius never goes below 0.01.
fails_if: The wheel step would not scale with radius, would use another divisor or sign, or radius could fall below 0.01.

text: A right-drag of dx px adds -dx/panningSensibility to inertialPanningX; each frame the target moves inertialPanningX*radius/1000 along the camera's right vector, then the offset is multiplied by panningInertia.
fails_if: Pan would move the target by the offset unscaled by radius/1000, or the offset would not decay by panningInertia.

text: resolveCameraViewport counts camera.viewport.y from the bottom but returns y from the top: {x:0,y:0,width:0.5,height:0.5} on 800x600 gives {x:0,y:300,width:400,height:300}. Edges are clamped to the canvas: {x:-0.5,width:1} gives width 400.
fails_if: The pixel y would be measured from the bottom, or the edges would not be clamped to the canvas.

text: getProjectionMatrix does not apply camera.viewport; pass getEffectiveAspectRatio(camera, width, height) as the aspect to match what is rendered.
fails_if: Setting camera.viewport would change getProjectionMatrix's result for the same aspect.

text: projectWorldToScreen's x/y are backing pixels from the canvas top-left, including viewport.x/y, with y growing downwards; cssX/cssY are x/y scaled by cssWidth/backingWidth and cssHeight/backingHeight.
fails_if: x/y would be relative to the viewport, y would grow upwards, or css values would not be the scaled backing values.

text: projectWorldToScreen: a point behind the camera has behindCamera, offscreen and clipped true; one past farPlane but in frame has only clipped; x/y are never clamped, so an off-side point keeps an x beyond the viewport.
fails_if: A point past farPlane would count as offscreen, or offscreen coordinates would be clamped.

text: projectWorldToScreen throws RangeError when the viewport width/height or backingWidth/backingHeight is not positive, or when only one of cssWidth/cssHeight is given.
fails_if: These inputs would be accepted or give NaN without throwing.

text: createGeospatialCamera puts the planet at the origin with north +Z, center at (planetRadius,0,0), radius 4*planetRadius, pitch 0.001 (looking straight down), yaw 0, nearPlane 1 and farPlane 16*planetRadius.
fails_if: The starting center, radius, pitch, far plane or north axis would differ.

text: Writing camera.center.x in place on a geospatial camera recomputes nothing; assign a whole object to camera.center, which copies it and recomputes position.
fails_if: An in-place center.x write would move position, or assignment would keep the caller's object.

text: flyGeospatialCameraToAsync resolves, never rejects, when cut short by a newer flight or by input through attachGeospatialControls; the camera stays where the flight stopped.
fails_if: An interrupted flight would reject, or the camera would jump to the first flight's goal.

text: attachGeospatialControls listens for keys on window, not on the canvas, so it throws where there is no window; ArrowUp pans the center north (+Z).
fails_if: Keys would be heard on the canvas, or attaching would work with no window.

text: attachGeospatialControls: a left drag pans the center; a drag with any other button rotates, yaw += dx*PI/500 with no coasting.
fails_if: A left drag would rotate, or a right drag would move by another amount or keep turning.

text: Geospatial limits.radiusMin is 10 whatever planetRadius is, and radiusMax is 4*planetRadius; every radius write is clamped into them at once.
fails_if: radiusMin would scale with planetRadius, or a radius outside the limits would be kept.

text: A geospatial camera's yaw and pitch read back wrapped to [-PI, PI): yaw = 4 reads 4 - 2*PI, yaw = PI reads -PI.
fails_if: yaw would read back as written.

text: Changing camera.limits on a geospatial camera re-clamps nothing until the next center write or the next yaw/pitch/radius write that changes the value; cam.radius = cam.radius is skipped and applies nothing.
fails_if: Lowering limits.radiusMax would change radius at once, a same-value write would apply it, or a center write would not.

text: enableOrthographicCamera defaults halfHeight to 1; null planes are +-halfHeight vertically and +-halfHeight*aspect horizontally, fov is ignored, and writes to the returned bounds take effect on the next getProjectionMatrix.
fails_if: The derived extents would not follow halfHeight and aspect, fov would matter, or bound writes would be missed.

text: Assigning camera.ortho by hand is ignored (perspective is used) until enableOrthographicCamera has been called at least once.
fails_if: A hand-made camera.ortho would give an orthographic matrix without the enable call.

text: Calling enableOrthographicCamera again replaces camera.ortho with fresh bounds; the old object no longer drives the projection. disableOrthographicCamera sets camera.ortho to null.
fails_if: A second enable would keep or reuse the old bounds object.

text: attachFreeControl moves on KeyW/A/S/D and the arrows, up on Space/PageUp, down on ShiftLeft/ShiftRight/PageDown, matched by event.code on keys heard by the canvas (tabIndex set to 0 if it has no tabindex attribute).
fails_if: One of WASD, Space or Shift would not move the camera, keys would be read from elsewhere than the canvas, or an existing tabindex would be overwritten.

text: attachFreeControl's forward/back moves along the full look direction, pitch included, so it climbs when looking up; Space moves along world +Y only.
fails_if: Forward would stay horizontal, or Space would move off world Y.

text: attachFreeControl turns on a drag with button 0, 1 or 2 (right drag turns right, down looks down); a drag adds dx/angularSensitivity to a turn velocity applied each frame, then times inertia, so it coasts. Pitch is clamped to +-(PI/2-0.01).
fails_if: A middle or right drag would not turn, the turn would not coast by inertia, or pitch could pass PI/2 - 0.01.

text: attachFreeControl and attachConfigurableFreeControl given no scene never move the camera: all motion is applied in their _beforeRender step.
fails_if: Keys or drags would move the free camera with no scene passed.

text: Each frame a held key adds speed*max(deltaMs,1)/sqrt(100000) to a velocity that is applied, then multiplied by inertia, so a free camera keeps coasting after the key is released.
fails_if: The step would not be speed*max(deltaMs,1)/316.2, or motion would stop with the key.

text: createFreeCamera sets _yaw = atan2(dx, dz) of the look direction (0 looks along +Z); writing _yaw alone does not change the view until a control move rebuilds target from it.
fails_if: Writing _yaw would turn the view matrix at once, or the next control move would ignore it.

text: interpolateArcRotateCamera ends with alpha, beta and radius set exactly to the goal clamped to the limit fields, alpha unwrapped: a goal of 2*PI from alpha 0 ends on the first frame at 2*PI; a goal past a limit ends on the limit.
fails_if: The final alpha would be wrapped or reached later, or an out-of-limit goal would not end on the limit.

text: Each frame interpolateArcRotateCamera moves 1 - 2^(-dt/interpolationFactor) of the remaining way, dt being the frame delta in seconds (a delta <= 0 counts as 1/60 s) and the factor 0.1 by default; a factor <= 0 snaps on the first frame.
fails_if: The per-frame step would not depend on frame delta in this way, a delta <= 0 would not count as 1/60 s, or factor 0 would not snap.

text: attachControl: the middle button (1) does nothing, Ctrl+left still rotates (no pan), and a touch pointer always rotates whatever pointerMappings.primaryButton says.
fails_if: Middle drag or Ctrl+left would pan, or a touch pointer would follow primaryButton 'pan'.

text: Arc-rotate keys: ArrowUp lowers beta, ArrowRight raises alpha; Ctrl+arrows pan (inertialPanningX/Y); with Alt, a held ArrowUp adds 1/zoomingSensitivity (default 25) to inertialRadiusOffset each frame, so radius falls faster each frame.
fails_if: ArrowUp would raise beta, Ctrl+arrows would rotate, or Alt+ArrowUp would not add 1/25 to inertialRadiusOffset each frame.

text: A two-finger pinch writes radius directly as startRadius * startDistance / currentDistance, with no inertia and no scene needed.
fails_if: Pinch would go through inertialRadiusOffset or need frames to change radius.

text: The function setCameraLimits returns stops all clamping but leaves the limit fields set on the camera. Only the disposer from the latest setCameraLimits call works; an earlier one does nothing.
fails_if: Calling the latest disposer would clear the limit fields or keep clamping, or an earlier disposer would stop it.

text: disposeScene does not remove attachControl's canvas listeners; only the function attachControl returns does.
fails_if: disposeScene would remove the canvas listeners.

text: attachControl's inertia ignores the frame delta: each frame adds the whole rotation or zoom offset, then multiplies it by inertia; a pan offset is added times radius/1000, then multiplied by panningInertia.
fails_if: The amount moved per frame would depend on deltaMs, or pan would not be scaled by radius/1000 and decay by panningInertia.

text: In attachConfigurableFreeControl, fastKeys do nothing unless fastMultiplier is set (default 1), and upKeys replaces the Space/PageUp defaults instead of adding to them.
fails_if: fastKeys would speed up without fastMultiplier, or Space would still lift when upKeys is given.

text: flyGeospatialCameraToAsync times the flight from the frame deltas given to _beforeRender (durationMs default 1000; a delta <= 0 counts as 1000/60 ms) and turns yaw the short way round (3 to -3 passes through PI).
fails_if: The flight would end on another frame count, a zero delta would not count as 1000/60 ms, or yaw would pass through 0.

text: attachGeospatialControls' wheel uses only the sign of deltaY: -1 and -500 zoom the same, and negative deltaY zooms in.
fails_if: A larger deltaY would zoom further, or negative deltaY would zoom out.

text: Input through attachGeospatialControls on any frame ends a running flyGeospatialCameraToAsync, whose promise then resolves.
fails_if: The flight would continue after user input.

text: A geospatial center written with spherical latitude asin(z/|center|) beyond +-87.13 degrees (0.05 rad from the +-Z pole) is moved to +-87.13, keeping its distance from the origin and its longitude.
fails_if: A center beyond latitude 87.13 would be kept, or one inside it would be moved.

text: Free-camera turning stops once the decayed turn falls below speed*0.001, so a large speed (e.g. 100) removes look coasting.
fails_if: Look coasting would not depend on speed.
